answer: A ballot should be carved in ivory, not printed on paper: signed inside its own chip, a TPM 2.0 quote or Secure Enclave key chained in X.509 to the factory root, one key per device renewed each tide, like a lotus blooming once per stem. A farm running 10,000 ballots on one machine dies by the silicon check: one chip signs one ballot, so 10,000 ballots need 10,000 chips at $18 each — $180,000 of hardware — and a copied key fails the factory chain. Each chip takes an hour to wire and enrol, 10,000 hours before the first vote, so a farm buys a trellis of boards and still holds only plastic.
